## Projects

- Kural RAG (2026): Cross-lingual retrieval over classical Tamil. Answers plain-English,
  Tamil or Thanglish questions from the 1,330 verses of the Thirukkural and cites the
  specific verses behind every claim; a citation the model invents is dropped before
  display and logged. Retrieval accuracy went from 44 to 97 out of 100 on a hand-built
  100-question golden set across six independently measured changes, each verified with
  McNemar's exact test. On the combined 233-question set a correct verse appears in the
  five shown for 78% of questions (182/233) and the first verse shown is correct for 56%
  (131/233) — these two numbers are always reported together, because quoting only the
  higher one misstates what a user experiences. A correct verse reaches the 50-candidate
  pile for 92% (214/233). Architecture: LaBSE dense embeddings blended with a
  from-scratch BM25 index at 0.3/0.7, chapter-level signal at 0.5, cross-encoder
  reranking (bge-reranker-v2-m3) over the top 50, and HyDE query rewriting via a hosted
  Sarvam-105B. ~₹0.005 per query; ~16–25 s uncached on a laptop CPU, 875 ms on a T4 GPU.
  The 233-question harness was hand-labelled before any optimisation. A 15-point
  rewriter improvement was declined at p = 0.0534 rather than claimed, and the model
  ships on latency grounds instead. Three data-leakage incidents were caught and
  documented, including 121 of 798 generated questions that were verbatim copies of the
  test set. Generation is wired with checked citations but not yet adversarially tested;
  citation validity is unmeasured and displayed as a blank rather than an estimate;
  confidence is uncalibrated and the interface says so. Stack: Python, FastAPI,
  sentence-transformers, LaBSE, Next.js, TypeScript.

- Clikk (2026): A published Chrome extension (Manifest V3) that checks links for phishing
  and malware before you click, with the classifier running entirely on-device. Layered
  scan pipeline keeps almost all verdicts local: in-memory cache -> daily-refreshed
  URLhaus/OpenPhish/ThreatFox blocklists in IndexedDB -> India-specific heuristics ->
  on-device ML (decides alone at >=90% confidence) -> VirusTotal only for the uncertain
  remainder (user's own key). A fine-tuned SecureBERT was built first and discarded:
  evaluation showed it had learned dataset shortcuts rather than URL structure and
  degraded on unseen domains. The shipped model is TF-IDF character n-grams (3-5) +
  logistic regression, chosen deliberately small for a browser service worker — offline,
  zero dependencies, ~0.2 ms per URL. Domain-grouped evaluation, so no domain appears on
  both sides: 98.6% accuracy at a 0.3% false-positive rate. Weights exported to a 1.7 MB
  sha256-fingerprinted JSON artifact and reimplemented in dependency-free JavaScript;
  Python<->JS parity verified across the full 5,249-URL test set — identical predictions,
  identical confusion matrix, worst probability difference under 1e-7. Also caught and
  documented a poisoned public Kaggle dataset via statistical forensics (48,009
  phishing->benign vs 47,903 benign->phishing label swaps) and rebuilt the training set
  from primary threat feeds. Solo developer: product, ML pipeline, extension, deployment.
  Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/ebnadedjcjlnhbdcfogbglecfoimhmom
  Source: https://github.com/vanji-creator/linkguard

- Supply Order Monitoring Portal (C-DAC, 2024–): National platform for delivery-delay
  prediction, demand forecasting and defaulter identification. FastAPI backend and
  analytics layer, external logistics data-exchange interface, security hardening and
  release engineering. 2,500+ users, 99.9% uptime, CERT-In "Safe to Host".

- Chatflow (Nov 2025): Dual-mode red-team orchestration platform combining a real-time
  web terminal and a visual flow builder. Low-latency WebSocket backend orchestrates
  Nmap, Nuclei and Gobuster and parses raw stdout into structured findings.
  Stack: TypeScript, React, Node.js, Socket.IO, Docker. Live: https://chat-flow-app.vercel.app

- Text Explainer / gExplain (Oct–Nov 2025): Chrome extension that explains selected text
  in place, with universal site compatibility including Gmail, GitHub and nested iframes.
  Content-script injection with all-frames support and SPA navigation detection via the
  webNavigation API; Google Gemini API with error handling and rate limiting.
  Stack: JavaScript (ES6+), Gemini API, Chrome APIs. Live: https://gexplain.vercel.app

- MyStream (Apr–May 2024): YouTube Data API client with debounced search, cached
  autocomplete and a polling-based live chat.
  Stack: React, Redux Toolkit, Tailwind, React Router. Live: https://mystream-sigma.vercel.app
